project_overview.what: The QS Revenue Dashboard pulls sales data from GoHighLevel (CRM) and turns it into a real-time performance dashboard. It tracks call volume, show rates, close rates, lead source attribution, rep-level performance, compliance, and funnel economics (RORI per rep once financial data is entered).
project_overview.why: Lloyd needs to see exactly how each sales rep is performing, which lead sources are producing revenue, and where the pipeline is leaking — without manually pulling GHL reports. This is the operational nervous system for the sales org.
project_overview.end_state: A comprehensive revenue intelligence platform with real-time KPIs, financial integration (Xero for actual revenue vs pipeline), automated anomaly detection, and API endpoints that feed the OpenClaw agent layer for cross-app synthesis.
project_overview.current_summary: Dashboard is live and in daily use across 5 tabs: Sales Performance, Lead Quality by Channel, Pipeline Intelligence, Funnel Economics, and Compliance. Xero invoice sync LIVE — Contract Value on P&L page updates monthly from actual ACCREC invoices with EUR→USD conversion. RORI columns display but require manual period financial inputs (Phase 2 will auto-pull from Xero). Show rate, compliance tracking, and lead quality distribution all working. Lloyd has real-time visibility into rep performance and pipeline economics.

known_issues.title: Scheduled incremental syncs stuck at 'running' + firing far too often (2026-06-17 → root-caused 2026-07-15)
known_issues.status: NEUTRALIZED AT DB LEVEL (2026-07-15, migration syncguard001): zombies survived the Railway restart (fired 23:23/23:25 UTC on old code while the new container demonstrably ran — leader lock held, :10 cron live, new ETA frontend serving) and the Supabase pooler masks client IPs so their host is unfindable via pg_stat_activity. Fix: BEFORE INSERT trigger on sync_runs rejects any status='running' row whose backend doesn't hold pg_advisory_xact_lock(728455002) — only current code takes that lock, so outdated processes anywhere are refused at run-creation (before any GHL work). Verified live: lock-less INSERT rejected, lock-holding INSERT allowed. Zombie hosts still worth locating for hygiene (check ALL Railway services/environments + old deployments; ask Geri if he runs the app anywhere pointed at prod Supabase)
known_issues.resolution: Root cause: MULTIPLE app processes ran schedulers at once — orphaned OLD-code containers each firing their own boot-relative hourly IntervalTrigger (stable offsets :23:17 / :25:03 / earlier :27:19) alongside the correct new 6h-cron process (:10). Confirmed via sync_runs timestamps + git (the :10 cron proves the fix is live; the hourly offsets are stale processes). Old code also predates the concurrency guard, so the parallel runs never skipped and piled up 'running'. CODE FIX (committed 2026-07-15): advisory-lock leader election (one scheduler process), atomic pg_advisory_xact_lock guard on both fresh + resume paths, graceful shutdown that cancels the in-flight sync so redeployed containers exit, leader-boot orphan heal. REMAINING (ops, not code — a deploy cannot stop an already-running process): hard-restart the Railway service to kill the live zombie containers; verify no second host via the restart-test (any non-:10 incremental after a clean restart = another host running the old scheduler).

known_issues.resolution: This working copy IS the standalone deploy repo: `origin` = git@github.com:lloyd-yip/qs-revenue-dashboard (app at repo ROOT, no qs-dashboard/ subtree here). Railway watches origin/main and auto-deploys on push (~1-2 min; verified live 2026-07-30 by polling /deals/collections 404→200). Alembic migrations are applied manually against Supabase (`alembic upgrade head` locally = prod, since .env DATABASE_URL points at prod); use idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`.

decision_log.decision: The company-wide CEO dashboard (/company) is built by STAGE, composing only data already in the DB first, then adding live inflow rails one at a time. Stage 1 (built 2026-08-06) reuses existing queries — no new sync, no schema change: live cash inflow = Whop net cash + bank wires (Wise/Payoneer summed from xero_bank_transfers, EUR→USD); plus the Collections snapshot, who-still-owes (payment-plan installments due/overdue), and the reconciled Xero P&L. The composing layer db/queries/company.py::get_company_overview calls the owning query fns (get_whop_live_summary_for_month, get_collections_for_range, get_bank_inflow_for_range, get_revenue_for_period/get_expenses_for_period) — no metric is recomputed. Later: Stage 2 live Stripe (incl. GHL sub-account subscriptions + commissions), Stage 3 direct Payoneer, Stage 4 affiliate — each written into revenue_line_items under a new source and surfaced as a new live_inflow channel.
decision_log.reasoning: Scott (CEO) wants accurate real-time cash inflow for the month across ALL channels, not just Whop. Today only Whop is live; Stripe is match-only (>$100 deal charges, so GHL sub-account subscriptions are deliberately filtered out and never counted as cash), affiliate is greenfield, and Payoneer/Wise incoming exists ONLY via the manual monthly Xero bank feed. The user chose to stage it ('implement everything we already have, add missing connections stage by stage'). Xero stays RECONCILED-only and clearly labelled on the page — the standing 'never present unreconciled Xero as live' decision is preserved (Xero is only accurate ~10 days after month-close). 'Who owes' = payment-plan installments due/overdue (the existing collections projection), the actionable list for a CEO. KNOWN CAVEAT (surfaced on the page): a wire that also settles a Collections deal can overlap the bank-wire line, so the combined live total is directional until a per-rail dedupe lands. New endpoints follow the browser-facing no-auth convention of the dashboard/whop_live routers (the page calls them without a bearer token); this diverges from the CLAUDE.md 'bearer auth on all new endpoints' checklist but matches every sibling read endpoint the page relies on — revisit if these read routes are ever locked down as a group.

decision_log.decision: Whop products are mapped to an editable CATEGORY (whop_product_mappings, Deals › Products tab) that decides whether their payments count as deal revenue: normal_deal + upsell COUNT; hermes (Calendar Automation) + ignore (one-off offers) are EXCLUDED. The matcher upserts the catalogue each run and builds its excluded-product set from these categories; auto_product_category seeds new products by name, is_manual pins a human override so the auto-mapper never clobbers it. This REPLACES the hardcoded EXCLUDED_WHOP_PRODUCT_IDS / name-pattern approach (those remain only as a static fallback seed).
decision_log.reasoning: Calendar Automation ships as many product IDs (per-tier + ARCHIVE variants) and new offers launch over time; hardcoding IDs meant a new CA tier silently counted as coaching (paul.walsh case: a CA product prod_QRBbImc0avOvr wasn't in the list). Lloyd wanted to read the product NAME to auto-exclude and to adjust the mapping himself, plus bucket products into Normal Deal / Hermes / Upsell. A stored, user-editable mapping is the right generalisation: auto-map by name, let Lloyd correct, and drive exclusion + (future) per-bucket reporting from one source of truth. NOTE: the basic Whop /products API doesn't expose price/all-time-revenue/active-users (price is per-plan; the others are dashboard-computed), so those display columns are blank for now — categorization is unaffected.

decision_log.decision: Sibling-fold eligibility also anchors on the MATCHED membership's own created_date (±SIBLING_SPLIT_WINDOW_DAYS=75), not just the GHL close date (±60). A customer settling one deal across memberships created weeks apart, or a deal with a missing/garbage close date, now folds correctly. ZeroMils, Kurt, abdul, ryan were reconciled by hand where auto-fold couldn't reach; paul.walsh's $17,634 was found to be a Stripe match (not Whop CA) and left for Lloyd's call.
decision_log.reasoning: abdul (two $3,850 Splitit charges) never folded because his GHL close date was a 2017 data-entry error, so the ±60d close-date window pointed at the wrong year; ryan's two Splitit charges were ~2 months apart, outside ±60d of close. Anchoring on the membership created_date (always reliable, Whop-native) with a slightly wider 75d split window catches both while an unrelated old purchase still fails both windows. Verified: a full 221-deal diff showed only abdul→$7,700 and ryan→$19,975 changed, zero collateral. Manual reconciliations: ZeroMils is a $15k deal (3×$5k, all count) not the stored $30k/$20k-refund; Kurt/ap-fleetsoft's confirmed $19,995 had whop_membership_id=NULL so its duplicate orphan never cleared (linked mem_xZMGjowADkcIiy). paul.walsh: Whop shows only Calendar Automation + $0, but the dashboard's $17,634 comes from a Stripe payment stream (stripe_email_exact) — $17,634 is a common plan price across 7 distinct customers (not a mis-match), so it's plausibly real card-paid coaching; whether to count it is Lloyd's decision.

decision_log.decision: A Whop membership whose payments are FOLDED into a deal (sibling-fold: one customer settling one deal across multiple memberships, e.g. Splitit split over cards) must be registered in claimed_by_membership so orphan detection never files it as a phantom 'Whop payment to attribute'. Applied in both the auto-match path and the confirmed-match path; the confirmed path claims siblings on EVERY run (independent of the enrich gate) so already-enriched confirmed deals stop re-orphaning. Correctness is delegated to the matcher (it re-folds from real Whop payment→membership data); phantom cleanup is authoritative via delete_claimed_orphans — never arithmetic-delete orphans by inferring from aggregate totals.
decision_log.reasoning: Discovered via kelsey.wang@primera-corp.com showing twice on New Deals: one $8.5k membership matched to Alex's Primera deal (with the $20k sibling folded in → $28,500) AND the $20k membership as a separate pending orphan. The orphan was a DUPLICATE of cash already counted, not extra money — my first read (that it was a separate $48.5k under-count) was wrong; the customer's total was $28,500, already fully on the deal. Root cause: sibling folding recorded only the PRIMARY membership as claimed, so _detect_orphans saw the folded sibling as unclaimed. Every split-Splitit deal spawned a phantom (same root as the wikifri/polarinsight cases). Confirming a phantom would double-count. Verified fix on prod: run-match dropped pending orphans 21→11, removed 10 phantom duplicates, and left every confirmed deal's total untouched (confirmed cash is never recomputed — early-return guards it). The 11 survivors are legitimate (7 have no GHL deal; 4 are genuinely-separate same-customer memberships the matcher deliberately did NOT fold — those need a human confirm/ignore/merge call, not auto-deletion). KEY LESSON: without a Whop key locally, only the matcher (which has per-payment membership mapping) can authoritatively decide folded-vs-separate — aggregate arithmetic can't distinguish 'own installments' from 'folded sibling'.

decision_log.decision: Collections-tab refunds are attributed to the month the refund was INITIATED (last_refund_date), not the deal's first-payment month; and the new per-rep commission worksheet commissions on GROSS cash collected minus refunds-this-window. Refund date is captured from the Whop payment's refunded_at; when absent it falls back to the deal's first-payment month (prior behaviour), so the change is safe pre-backfill.
decision_log.reasoning: Lloyd asked whether a refund should belong to the deal's first-payment month or the month it happened. Refund-date is more useful for a cash/commission view: a deal closed in Feb but refunded in May hits May, so already-reported months don't retroactively change and commission claws back in the month the refund lands. Commission uses GROSS (total_paid) to match the established comp model (metrics_by_rep commissions on total_paid) = how reps are actually paid; that's why the rep table's Cash Collected can exceed the net 'Collected' card (which is net of Whop provider fees). CAVEAT: the Whop refunded_at field name was NOT verifiable locally (no Whop key in the local .env); the capture is defensive (refunded_at + aliases) and degrades gracefully to the first-payment-month fallback if the field differs — verify on prod after a Whop refresh populates last_refund_date on the 4 known refunded deals.

decision_log.decision: Sync scheduler runs in exactly ONE process via a Postgres advisory-lock leader election; the run_sync concurrency guard is now ATOMIC (pg_advisory_xact_lock) and also covers the resume path; graceful shutdown cancels the in-flight sync so a redeployed container exits instead of lingering as a zombie. New module db/advisory_lock.py holds the leader key (session lock) + guard key (xact lock). Correctness comes from the DB-level xact guard (works even behind Supabase's transaction pooler); the session-level leader lock is a best-effort optimisation layered on top.
decision_log.reasoning: Duplicate hourly syncs (2026-07-14/15) came from orphaned OLD-code processes on the host — two stable hourly offsets (:23:17, :25:03; earlier :27:19) that never shifted across deploys = boot-relative IntervalTrigger processes (pre-e6c75a2), and both showing 'running' at once = pre-7b087ce (no guard). The 6h-cron fix and the guard were ALREADY committed and live (the :10 cron fires), which proves the extra syncs came from separate stale processes. KEY LESSON: a code deploy cannot stop an already-running process — it starts a NEW process and leaves the old one running its old timer. So the code fix prevents RECURRENCE (leader election + atomic guard + graceful shutdown make it structurally impossible once every process is on the new code), but the LIVE zombies must be killed at the host (Railway hard-restart), and a second host (e.g. Render) must be ruled out via a restart-test (any non-:10 incremental after a clean restart = another host).

decision_log.decision: Three Whop payment-model fixes (Freitag case): (1) nightly refresh window widened from current-month to 190-day lookback so later installments keep stacking; (2) renewal-plan projection — recurring memberships (e.g. $6,000/3-months) have no split_pay_required_payments, so once >=2 installments land, plan length is inferred as ceil(GHL contract / avg installment) capped at 12 (GHL used as COUNT hint only; single-payment deals never inflated; stale stored plan lengths smaller than payment_count are discarded; total_installments grows monotonically on refresh); (3) duplicate-membership dedupe — one membership's payments belong to ONE deal; when two GHL won deals match the same membership, the stronger method wins (manual > email_exact > email_domain > fuzzy) and the loser becomes unmatched with method 'duplicate_membership'.
decision_log.reasoning: wikifri.com: two duplicate GHL won deals (Bill Freitag / William K Freitag, $15k each) matched the same $6,000/3-months renewing membership — $6,000 double-counted, the Jul 14 renewal invisible (first payment Jun 11 fell outside the current-month refresh window), and projected total stuck at $6,000 because len(payments)=1 at match time. After fixes: William email_exact keeps the match (12,000 collected, projected 18,000), Bill demoted to duplicate_membership. NOTE: the duplicate GHL opportunity still inflates CLOSED counts — needs GHL-side cleanup (mark one as Duplicate).

decision_log.decision: Whop payment metrics aggregate at the CUSTOMER level, not just the matched membership ('sibling folding'). Payments from the customer's other memberships fold into the deal when: same email, membership not claimed by another deal, customer has no other matched deals, created within +/-60d of close date, payment paid and >$100. Applies in both the matching engine and the nightly whop-refresh (which now also corrects first_payment_date). Payment logic extracted to sync/whop_payments.py (matcher 1012->869 lines).
decision_log.reasoning: Splitit sometimes cannot approve the full contract on one card, so a customer completes one deal as two memberships (james@polarinsight.com: $18,000 quantumSCALE membership Jun 11 + separate $2,700 Splitit top-up Jul 6). Counting only the matched membership understated cash ($2,700 vs $20,700), projected total, first payment date, and sales cycle. The guards prevent double-counting when one customer legitimately has multiple deals (each claims its own membership) and exclude community subs via the $100 floor.

decision_log.decision: Rep tables get a payment-verified 'Projected Total' column (Whop plan math: financed Splitit/ClarityPay = total paid, settles 100% upfront; internal plans = avg installment x total_installments from split_pay_required_payments). Cash Collected switched from upfront_cash to total_paid so monthly installments stack as they land; commission accrues on cash-to-date. upfront_cash kept for the % Upfront metric.
decision_log.reasoning: The CONTRACT VALUE column is a passthrough of GHL monetary_value (rep-entered, match_deals_whop.py denormalizes it) and diverges wildly from payment reality (e.g. GHL $25k vs $8k actual plan). The Whop-derived projection needs no rep input and self-corrects. Cash-as-upfront never accumulated installments, understating collections and freezing commission at the first payment. Known rough edges: assumes equal installments; $0-paid matches project $0; partial Splitit settlements project low. Follow-up same day: basis aligned EVERYWHERE — lead_source (channel table + closes), funnel_economics (avg cash = total_paid; % upfront stays upfront), pipeline_intelligence segment closes (was raw GHL cash_collected), slwa closes, rep closes drill-down. All closes modals now show Deal Value (GHL) vs Cash Paid vs Projected Total side by side. Shared expr: db/queries/common.whop_projected_total_expr(). Second follow-up: PI segment TABLE also aligned (contract/cash were raw GHL opportunity fields — cash showed all dashes; now match-table basis + Projected Total column, consistent with rep/channel tables). Channel-table debug drill-downs added: every count cell (Total Opps, Shows, LQ grades) links to /debug?channel=...; money cells open the closes modal; new debug metric keys channel_total_opps/channel_shows/lq_* mirror lead_source exactly (verified counts match to the unit).

decision_log.decision: Rep cost is DERIVED from a per-rep comp model (rep_comp_settings: monthly base salary + commission % of cash collected; defaults $0 + 10%), not read from Xero 'sales' bucket payouts. Total Invested = prorated base + commission x cohort cash collected + marketing allocation. Editable in the new Sales Reps tab.
decision_log.reasoning: Xero payouts are cash-basis: with split payments, a rep's May payout reflects deals closed months earlier, so cost and revenue described different cohorts and RORI drifted. Deriving commission from cohort cash collected self-corrects — when an installment lands, both the numerator (cash) and denominator (commission cost) update together in the same window. Also fixes the silent gap where Armando (invoicing as J.A Valencia Enterprices LLC) never appeared in the Xero Salaries-Sales account, so his comp was $0. Xero payouts remain on the P&L/Expenses pages as actual cash out (reconciliation check).

decision_log.decision: Navigation consolidation: all 9 pages now use shared nav.js (single Tier-1 bar) — removed 4 divergent navbar implementations. Page-specific subnav handling (Sales 7-tab .subbar, Deals segmented lens, etc.) preserved via data-config, not separate HTML/JS.
decision_log.reasoning: Duplicate navbar code across pages created maintenance burden and UX inconsistency (some pages missing nav items). Single shared module reduces code duplication, centralizes nav state, and ensures visual/behavioral consistency. Sales 7-tab subbar + Deals segmented lens are preserved as page-level details, not part of shared Tier-1 nav. Shipped as commit 41def90 with design PASS (tokens exact, theme parity verified).

decision_log.decision: Phase 2 (Xero financial autopull) CANCELLED — Funnel Economics inputs remain manual. v1 DEALS REWORK LOCKED: relocate Live Whop to Deals page (2-lens toggle: Live default, Historical reconciled), rep fallback + Cash/Contract labels, month picker keyed to Whop data not P&L (fixes May/June unreachable).
decision_log.reasoning: Xero data is only accurate AFTER human reconciliation (~10-day lag post-month-close). Auto-pulling unreconciled numbers would feed the dashboard confidently-wrong figures every period — worse than transparent manual entry. The cash-collected half shipped as Whop Live Revenue (verified 2026-06-11). The spend/comp half is NOT a build — it's a data-accuracy gate. Funnel Economics is correctly a trailing/reconciled metric. v1 Deals redesign ships first (front-loads user-facing UX-fixes + unlocks May/June visibility); v2 monthly cash ledger (net-new vs recurring with recurring-decay model) fully spec'd in blueprints/monthly_cash_ledger_blueprint_v2.md but deferred. Mockup approved 2026-06-13.

decision_log.decision: Never auto-pull financials from Xero into the dashboard. Real-time inputs come from operational systems (Whop for cash, ad platforms for spend); Xero is reconciled-only.
decision_log.reasoning: Xero numbers are not accurate until a human reconciles them (~10-day lag) — the same lag that motivated the Whop Live Revenue feature. Auto-pulling unreconciled Xero would feed the dashboard confidently-wrong figures every period, which is worse than deliberate manual entry. This kills the originally-planned Phase 2 'Xero autopull'. RORI is a trailing metric (needs accurate costs), so its manual reconciled inputs are appropriate and stay manual. Live/now metrics (cash collected) use operational sources; trailing/reconciled metrics (RORI) tolerate the lag.

decision_log.decision: Whop processor detection is PAYMENT-level, not membership-level; net cash = total_paid x 0.85 for Splitit/ClarityPay, total_paid otherwise; internal-plan length from split_pay_required_payments
decision_log.reasoning: Verified against live Whop API 2026-06-11. ClarityPay is invisible on the membership (reads 'multi_psp'); only payment.payment_processor exposes 'claritypay'. Financed deals (Splitit/ClarityPay) settle 100% upfront as a single payment, so total_paid x 0.85 is correct from day one. Internal plans only record collected installments, so len(payments) under-counts — split_pay_required_payments is the authoritative plan length. Full model in knowledge/whop_payment_model.md.

decision_log.decision: Xero invoices are the authoritative source for contract value (not GHL projected_deal_size)
decision_log.reasoning: GHL projected_deal_size is unreliable — reps don't fill it in consistently. Xero ACCREC invoices reflect what was actually billed to clients.

decision_log.decision: Contract value stored as one aggregate row per month in revenue_line_items (source=xero, category=contract_value, product_type=invoiced_total)
decision_log.reasoning: Monthly aggregate is sufficient for RORI calculation. Per-deal invoice matching deferred to Phase 3 — adds fuzzy name matching complexity without changing the RORI formula.

decision_log.decision: Category-scoped DELETE before invoice upsert (not replace=True in upsert_revenue_line_items)
decision_log.reasoning: replace=True would wipe cash_collected rows for the same period. Category-scoped delete is surgical — only removes contract_value rows, leaving other categories intact.

decision_log.decision: Shared Xero helpers extracted to api/utils/xero_utils.py instead of xero_auth.py
decision_log.reasoning: xero_auth.py is already 1,107 lines. Adding to it risks further growth and creates router→router import coupling. New shared utils file is the clean boundary.

decision_log.decision: Show count numerator uses showed_1st_call_expr() alone — no compliance flag filter
decision_log.reasoning: compliance flags (outcome_unfilled, rep_compliance_failure) must never gate metric counts. A rep moving to the 'Call 1 Done' stage counts as a show regardless of whether appointment status field was also updated. Compliance flags are for separate compliance tab only.

decision_log.decision: RORI defined as Contract Value ÷ (Rep Comp + Mktg Alloc) for Contract RORI, Cash Collected ÷ (Rep Comp + Mktg Alloc) for Cash RORI
decision_log.reasoning: Marketing allocation per rep = (Total Mktg Spend ÷ Team Total Shows) × Rep Shows. This proportionally assigns shared marketing cost based on each rep's share of team volume.

decision_log.decision: Funnel Economics financial inputs are manually entered (not auto-pulled from Xero yet)
decision_log.reasoning: Xero/WAP API integration is Phase 2. Phase 1 validates the metric logic and UI with manual entry first. Once accounting data is confirmed correct, Phase 2 automates the feed.

decision_log.decision: qs-dashboard lives in monorepo locally but deploys from standalone qs-revenue-dashboard GitHub repo
decision_log.reasoning: Railway service was originally created from the standalone repo. Easiest to maintain — use git subtree push to keep qs-revenue-dashboard in sync with monorepo changes.

decision_log.decision: Incremental sync every 6 hours (01:10/07:10/13:10/19:10 UTC cron), not hourly — SUPERSEDES the hourly cadence (2026-07-14). Daily Fireflies appointment resolver at 7pm EST and Sunday full sync unchanged.
decision_log.reasoning: Each incremental makes per-opportunity GHL calls (~35 min, thousands of requests); 24 runs/day exhausted the 200k/day GHL quota on 2026-07-14, blocking manual full syncs (fatal 429s) and starving all other GHL usage. 4 runs/day keeps data at most ~6.5h stale — acceptable — with ample quota headroom. Fixed clock times replace the boot-relative interval so deploys don't re-phase the cadence. GHL client 429 backoff also hardened (8 attempts, exponential to 2 min). Follow-up candidate: make the incremental itself cheaper (per-opp appointment/notes lookups are the request burner).

decision_log.decision: Show/no-show detection via union of appointment status + pipeline stage signals
decision_log.reasoning: No single GHL field reliably indicates show/no-show. Union of signals catches more cases than either alone.

decision_log.decision: Bearer token auth on all API endpoints
decision_log.reasoning: Simple, sufficient for internal tool. Upgrade to JWT/API key scoping when cross-app orchestration needs differentiated access.

feature_backlog.title: Relocate Live Whop view from P&L to Deals page
feature_backlog.problem: The live per-rep Whop cash view is buried at the bottom of the P&L (money-summary) page. To see live deal-level activity Lloyd has to open P&L, when it belongs alongside the historical deal reconciliation on the Deals page. CRITICAL UX FLAW (2026-06-11): the Live Whop section is chained to the P&L period dropdown, which is populated from months with P&L data loaded (revenue_line_items/expenses), NOT from months with Whop deals. The dropdown stops at Apr 2026; May/June Whop deals exist in the DB but are UNREACHABLE, and the live view cannot show the current month — undercutting its real-time purpose.
feature_backlog.why_important: P&L is the financial summary; Deals is where deal-level detail lives. Splitting live deals onto P&L makes the information architecture confusing and the live view hard to find. Lloyd explicitly requested the move (2026-06-11).
feature_backlog.user_story: When I open the Deals page, I expect to switch between historical/reconciled deals and live/this-month deals in one place. Currently: reconciled deals are on the Deals page, but live this-month deals are on a separate P&L page.
feature_backlog.success_definition: The Deals page shows a Historical/Live toggle; the Live lens renders the per-rep collapsible Whop view (net cash, contract, fee + confidence badges); the P&L page no longer contains the Live Whop section.
acceptance_criteria: Deals page (static/deals.html) has a visible toggle/tabs switching between 'Historical (Reconciled)' and 'Live (This Month)'
Live lens renders per-rep collapsible buckets with net cash, gross contract, Splitit/ClarityPay -15% badges, HIGH/MEDIUM confidence badges, and an 'as of ... refreshed nightly' line
Live lens shows the correct empty state for a month with no Whop deals (does not error)
P&L page (static/pnl.html) no longer renders #whop-live-section and no longer calls loadWhopLive
GET /api/dashboard/pnl/whop-live still returns 200 and drives the Live lens unchanged

Live lens has its OWN month selector populated from months that have Whop deals (deal_whop_matches.first_payment_date), defaulting to the CURRENT month — decoupled from the P&L revenue-period dropdown so recent/current months (e.g. May/June 2026) are always reachable
A rep's deals are findable without hunting month-by-month — the Live lens makes the active month obvious and/or offers a rep-centric view spanning months (decide in /ux-design)
feature_backlog.general_approach: Pure frontend relocation. Move loadWhopLive/renderWhopLiveSection/renderRepBucket + the Live Whop CSS from pnl.html into deals.html. Add a lens toggle on the Deals page: 'Historical' = existing reconciliation cards/table, 'Live' = the relocated Whop view (calls the existing GET /pnl/whop-live for the current month). Remove the #whop-live-section block + loadWhopLive call from pnl.html. No backend change.
